heading: Before & after
lead: Read this before your session. Come back to it when you need it.

items.title: Well-rested body
items.text: Show up rested. Sessions on no sleep are sessions you'll regret.

items.title: Food
items.text: Eat a proper meal within two hours before your arrival. Low blood sugar makes long sessions miserable.

items.title: Hydration
items.text: Drink water through the day. Avoid alcohol for 24 hours before — it thins your blood.

items.title: Clothing
items.text: Loose, dark clothing that gives easy access to the area being tattooed.

items.title: Distraction
items.text: Headphones, a downloaded show, a book. Long sessions need a way to vanish into your head.

items.title: Snacks & water
items.text: Bring something to eat and drink for breaks. Keep some simple sugars on hand for a quick energy boost if you start feeling faint.

after.title: Aftercare

phases.label: Day 0 — the first night
body: Leave the wrap on until you get home or to a hotel. Wash yourself, then wash the tattooed area gently with lukewarm water and a fragrance-free soap. Pat dry with a clean paper towel. Do not rub. Apply a thin layer of
. Sleep on clean sheets. Wear loose clothing over the area.

phases.label: Days 1-3
body: Wash and re-wrap ideally every 4 hours. Apply a thin layer of an unscented healing balm like
. The tattoo will weep plasma and ink — this is normal. Sleep on clean sheets. Wear loose clothing over the area.

phases.label: Days 4-14
body: It will scab and flake. Do not pick, scratch, or peel. Keep moisturising with an unscented lotion of your choice. Itch is normal — slap, don't scratch. No pools, no baths, no saunas, no sea.

phases.label: Weeks 2-6
body: The surface heals first, the deeper skin takes longer. Stay out of direct sun if possible. Once fully healed, use SPF 50+ on the tattoo any time it sees sunlight — this is the single biggest thing you can do to keep it sharp for decades.

donts: Keep it out of the sun for the first two weeks. No tanning beds, either.
No pools, baths, sea, or saunas for at least two weeks.
No scented lotions or vaseline on a fresh tattoo.
No gym sessions that stretch or sweat-soak the area for the first week.

items.title: Buy baby products
body: Everything you need for aftercare exists in the baby aisle, and it costs a fraction of what tattoo-branded products charge for the same thing. Bepanthen started as a nappy rash cream. The absorbing pads are baby changing mats. The skin does not know the difference.

items.title: Skip second skin
body: I don't use second skin on my clients. I had a bad experience with a contaminated batch with which people got infections. Even without that, some skin simply doesn't tolerate it. Baby pads, on the other hand, everybody tolerates.

items.title: Finding the right pad
body: Head to the diaper aisle and look at the packaging. When it stops listing weight in kg and starts listing size in centimetres — something like 60x60 cm — that's the one you want. Those are the changing mats. They absorb exactly the same as any pad sold in a tattoo shop.

items.title: Moisturise beforehand
body: Hydrate the target area once or twice a day for 1-2 weeks before your appointment with a fragrance-free, unscented lotion. Soft, elastic skin holds ink more evenly and tears less under the needle. Day of the session: skip the lotion entirely. Any residue interferes with the stencil transfer and creates hygiene problems.

items.title: If it looks infected
body: — spray directly on the area, let it air dry. Do
use antiseptic spray with alcohol. Alcohol dries out the skin and can pull ink from the dermis.

page.subtitle: Read this before your session. Come back to it when you need it for two weeks after. Bookmark it.
